fields.reasoning: Milestone 25 is the open milestone and its intent is building and shipping the queued owner requests; this change set's intent is one of those requests, so it serves milestone-25. On main: the question states ship-change rebases a PR that main has moved past and merges only a head whose checks passed, so with squash merges the merge commit's tree equals the tested head's tree; comparing trees keeps the guarantee wait-main gave (main is what was tested) without the CI run the change set removes, and failing loudly on a mismatch keeps a real gap visible instead of silently passing. On the template: cancelling superseded PR runs is safe for any repo, but dropping the main check is only safe where a merge tool guarantees the merged tree was tested, which ci install cannot assume about other repos. On landing: memory and the question both say the agents' gh token lacks the `workflow` scope, so any agent push touching .github/workflows/ is rejected and would stall the run; keeping the workflow edit out of agent leaves lets the Go work ship through ship-change, and ordering the hand edit after it means main never stops testing while ship still waits on main runs.
fields.statement: (1) The change set serves milestone-25 (empty the backlog): it is an owner request from the queue, and cheaper, non-redundant CI helps the daemon ship the backlog on its own. (2) Main stops running CI on push, and ship-change stops waiting for CI on main: the wait-main step (`rhiza ship check --main --settled`) instead passes when the merge commit's tree equals the tree of the PR head whose checks passed, checked locally with git and no wait on GitHub; if the trees differ it fails with a stop: line for a look, and never waits an hour for runs that will not come. (3) Both change: this repo's .github/workflows/ci.yml drops the push-to-main trigger and gains a concurrency group per pull request with cancel-in-progress; the `rhiza ci install` template in internal/api/ci.go gains the same cancel-stale concurrency group, but keeps its push-to-main check, since other repos may merge by hand without ship-change's tested-tree guarantee. (4) The agents' leaves change only Go code (ship check, the ci.go template, tests, golden files) and never touch .github/workflows/. The ci.yml edit is left to the owner to commit and push by hand with a token that has the `workflow` scope, after the ship-check change has landed; the change set records it as a question or note for the owner rather than a leaf an agent builds.
